title: Guest Bathroom Quick Prep: Get It Ready in 15 Minutes (Plus 7 Amazon Finds)
description: Guests coming soon? A 15-minute guest bathroom prep for busy brains, a ready-to-go guest basket and 7 Amazon finds that make it easy every time.
intro:
Someone texts "on our way!" and our first thought is: the bathroom. The one with toothpaste on the sink, an empty toilet paper roll and a towel of questionable age.

The guest bathroom is where people are alone with your stuff, so it gets a lot of our worry. The good news: it's also the smallest room to fix. With a little setup now, getting it guest-ready takes 15 minutes, even on short notice.

Here's the quick-prep routine, a guest basket you can grab and set out, and seven Amazon finds that make the whole thing easier.

sections.heading: The 15-minute guest bathroom prep
sections.body:
Set a timer and go in this order. Top to bottom, so dust and drips fall onto spots you haven't cleaned yet.

1. **Clear the counter (3 minutes).** Everything that isn't soap goes into a bin. Put the bin under the sink or in your bedroom.
2. **Mirror and faucet (2 minutes).** One cleaning wipe for both. Shiny faucets make the whole room look clean.
3. **Toilet (4 minutes).** Wipe the seat, lid and handle. Swish the bowl with a brush.
4. **Swap the hand towel (1 minute).** A fresh towel instantly says "ready for guests."
5. **Toilet paper check (1 minute).** One on the holder, two visible extras.
6. **Trash and floor (4 minutes).** Empty the trash and pick up anything on the floor. Quick sweep or wipe if there's time.

sections.heading: Make a 'guest-ready' basket
sections.body:
This is the trick that makes prep fast every time. Fill one small basket with:

- A fresh hand towel
- Spare toilet paper
- A small bottle of hand soap
- A spare toothbrush and travel toothpaste
- A few hair ties and some cotton pads

Keep the basket in the linen closet. When guests are coming, carry it in and set it on the counter or the back of the toilet. When they leave, refill it and put it back.

sections.heading: Make toilet paper easy to find
sections.body: Guests won't open your cabinets, so hiding extra rolls under the sink means a very awkward text from the bathroom. Keep spare rolls out in the open in a simple stand or basket. It's one less thing to worry about.

sections.heading: Keep cleaning stuff in the bathroom
sections.body: If the cleaning supplies live in the kitchen, the bathroom prep feels like a whole expedition. Stash wipes, a toilet brush and a small spray bottle right in the bathroom. When it's in reach, a 2-minute wipe can happen whenever you notice it.

sections.heading: Little touches guests notice
sections.body: You don't need to decorate. One or two small things make the room feel cared for: a candle or air freshener, a little plant (real or fake), and a hook on the back of the door for guests' things. Done.

outro:
A guest bathroom doesn't need to be spotless. It needs a clear counter, a clean towel and toilet paper people can find. With a basket ready to go, that's a 15-minute job.

If the rest of the house could use the same zone-by-zone approach, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* breaks every room into small, doable steps.
